title: Add Two Numbers
keyIdea: The digits are stored backwards, so the first nodes are the ones digits. That's the order you add by hand: add column by column, write sum % 10, carry sum / 10 into the next column. Keep going while either list or the carry is left.

approaches.name: Convert to numbers
approaches.idea: Read each list into a number, add the two numbers, then write the sum back out as a list, ones digit first.
approaches.why: One pass over each list and one pass over the sum's digits.
approaches.warn: Wrong for big inputs: a list can have 100 digits, but long long only holds about 19. It overflows, so mention it and move on.

approaches.name: Column addition with carry
approaches.idea: Walk both lists together. Each step: sum = carry + l1 digit (if any) + l2 digit (if any). Append sum % 10 to the answer, carry = sum / 10. A dummy node means the first digit is appended like every other one.
approaches.why: One loop iteration per column, and there are at most max(m, n) + 1 columns. Apart from the answer list itself, only sum, carry and a few pointers.

quiz.q: Why is it handy that the digits are stored in reverse order?
options: The first nodes are the ones digits, so you can add and carry in the same order you walk the lists
It means there's never a carry
It lets you sort the digits
1, because a column is at most 9 + 9 + 1 = 19
It depends on the list length

quiz.q: Why does the while loop also check carry != 0?
options: When both lists end with a carry left (999 + 1), one more node is needed for that 1

quiz.q: l1 has run out but l2 still has digits. What does the code use for l1's digit?
options: Nothing is added, which is the same as adding 0

quiz.q: Why return dummy->next instead of dummy?
options: dummy is a placeholder 0 at the front that isn't part of the answer
